houston.intro: Houston's heat, flooding, and energy economy make AI's energy footprint, environmental data, and public-service decisions immediate local questions. The city's resilience reporting identifies environmental justice and community engagement as priorities; these readings ask who is represented, protected, and able to challenge automated decisions.

readings.title: Resilient Houston: Three-Year Report
readings.note: The report tracks city resilience work, environmental justice, and efforts to measure inequities. It is local context, not an AI policy.

readings.title: Atlas of AI: Power, Politics, and the Planetary Costs of Artificial Intelligence
readings.note: Connects AI to energy, mineral extraction, data labor, and environmental costs—useful questions for an energy-intensive region.

tokyo.intro: Tokyo's metropolitan AI guidelines give public servants practical direction for adopting AI across agencies and engaging diverse stakeholders. Consider how human responsibility, privacy, explainability, and access for residents using different languages carry through from policy to deployment.

readings.title: Tokyo AI Adoption and Use Guidelines
readings.source: Tokyo Metropolitan Government · Bureau of Digital Services
readings.note: The metropolitan framework covers appropriate AI adoption in government and engagement with diverse stakeholders.

readings.title: AI Ethics
readings.note: An accessible introduction to accountability, values, and the social effects of AI beyond technology hype.

ja.intro: 東京都のAI利活用ガイドラインは、都庁各局でAIを適切に導入し、多様な関係者と協力するための実践的な指針です。政策を実際の運用につなげる際、人の責任、プライバシー、説明可能性、さまざまな言語を使う住民へのアクセスをどう守るかを考えます。

readings.title: Tokyo AI Adoption and Use Guidelines
readings.source: 東京都 デジタルサービス局
readings.note: 都庁におけるAIの適切な導入と、多様な関係者との協力に関する指針です。

readings.title: AI Ethics
readings.note: 技術への過度な期待にとどまらず、AIの説明責任、価値観、社会への影響をわかりやすく解説します。

osaka.intro: Osaka City's AI utilization basic policy frames AI as a partner to public employees while emphasizing human oversight, citizen benefit, privacy, fairness, and safety. Research from the University of Osaka's ELSI Center adds questions about how people value AI in healthcare. Together, these sources connect local public services, Osaka's research community, and everyday trust in automated decisions.

readings.title: Osaka City AI Utilization Basic Policy
readings.note: Sets out 11 principles for responsible municipal AI use, including human oversight, fairness, privacy, and security.

readings.title: Design of a Q-sort method for evaluating people's values regarding the introduction of AI into healthcare (ELSI NOTE 67)
readings.source: The University of Osaka Research Center on Ethical, Legal and Social Issues
readings.note: Research from Osaka's ELSI Center on how people's values can inform decisions about introducing AI into healthcare.

ja.eyebrow: 大阪のリーディングリスト
ja.intro: 大阪市のAI活用基本方針は、AIを職員との共創パートナーとして位置付けながら、人による監督、市民の便益、プライバシー、公平性、安全性を重視しています。大阪大学ELSIセンターの研究は、医療AIに対する人々の価値観を考える視点を加えます。これらの資料は、地域の公共サービス、大阪の研究コミュニティ、自動化された判断への日常的な信頼を結び付けます。

readings.title: 大阪市AI活用基本方針
readings.note: 人による監督、公平性、プライバシー、セキュリティなど、自治体でAIを適切に活用するための11の原則を示しています。

readings.title: 医療へのAI導入に対する人々の価値観を評価するQソート法の設計（ELSI NOTE 67）
readings.source: 大阪大学 社会技術共創研究センター（ELSIセンター）
readings.note: 医療AIの導入を検討する際、人々の価値観をどのように捉えられるかを扱う大阪大学の研究です。

manchester.intro: Greater Manchester has a locally developed model for putting residents—especially people often left out of technology decisions—in the room with researchers and businesses. These readings connect that public participation work to practical questions for the region’s AI builders: who gets to challenge a system, whose experience shapes it, and who remains accountable when it is used.

readings.title: Greater Manchester People’s Panel for AI: Building Trust and Giving People a Voice
readings.note: A case-study booklet about Greater Manchester residents questioning AI research and products, and the changes that followed.

readings.title: Greater Manchester SME perspectives on current practices and future regulation of artificial intelligence
readings.source: Manchester Metropolitan University and Greater Manchester AI Foundry
readings.note: Research on how small and medium-sized businesses in Greater Manchester approach responsible AI and the challenges they face.

readings.title: The AI Con: How to Fight Big Tech’s Hype and Create the Future We Want
readings.source: Emily M. Bender and Alex Hanna · HarperCollins
readings.note: A critical account of AI industry claims that helps readers ask whose interests, labor and evidence are represented when systems are adopted.

nyc.intro: New York City publishes principles and guidance for government AI, while Local Law 144 sets requirements for automated employment decision tools. These sources connect public-service accountability with the practical question of how AI-based hiring systems affect New Yorkers.

readings.title: New York City Generative AI Use Guidance
readings.source: New York City Office of Technology and Innovation
readings.note: The city’s guidance applies its AI principles to generative-AI use, with questions about suitability, reliability, privacy and human responsibility.

readings.title: Automated Employment Decision Tools (Local Law 144)
readings.source: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
readings.note: Explains the city law’s bias-audit, public-summary and candidate-notice requirements for covered automated hiring tools.

readings.title: The Algorithm: How AI Decides Who Gets Hired, Monitored, Promoted, and Fired
readings.note: Investigates AI in recruiting and workplace decisions, adding a practical lens to New York’s rules for algorithmic hiring.

dallas.intro: A March 2025 City of Dallas committee briefing describes its AI plan around governance, applications and staff preparation. It says the City remains responsible for model outputs—especially when resources or benefits are allocated—and recommends human review and transparency. Read the briefing alongside the City’s current technology-accountability reporting and independent research on bias in automated systems.

readings.title: Update on Artificial Intelligence: City AI Plan, Governance and Best Practices
readings.source: City of Dallas · Government Performance and Financial Management Committee, March 2025
readings.note: The committee briefing outlines the City’s AI-plan priorities, discusses risks including bias, and recommends human oversight and transparency. It is a briefing, not a claim that every recommendation has become a binding citywide policy.

readings.title: Technology Accountability Report — August 2026
readings.source: City of Dallas Information and Technology Services
readings.note: The City’s report describes the status of technology purchasing, implementation, operations and security through August 31, 2026. It provides local oversight context; it is not an AI-specific policy.

readings.title: Race After Technology: Abolitionist Tools for the New Jim Code
readings.note: A research-based look at how technologies that appear neutral can hide or deepen discrimination—a useful lens for considering automated systems in public services.

stlouis.intro: St. Louis City's AI policy connects government use to privacy, cybersecurity, and Missouri's Sunshine Law. Its focus on transparency and accountability raises important questions about how residents can understand, question, and seek remedies for decisions that affect them.

readings.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy
readings.source: City of St. Louis · Information Technology Services
readings.note: The city policy addresses staff use of AI tools, privacy, cybersecurity, and compliance with Missouri Sunshine Law.

portland.intro: Portland's municipal AI rule aligns the acquisition and use of AI with city values including anti-racism, equity, transparency, and fiscal responsibility. These readings connect those commitments to oversight of automated public services and the people most affected by them.

readings.title: The City's approach to responsible use of AI
readings.note: Explains Portland's safeguards and responsible-use commitments for city staff using AI.

readings.title: Automating Inequality: How High-Tech Tools Profile, Police, and Punish the Poor
readings.note: Investigates how automated systems in public programs can deepen surveillance and inequality.

bulverde.intro: Bulverde's stormwater program and regional aquifer data make environmental monitoring a concrete local context for ethical AI questions. If automated tools inform water-quality or planning decisions, ask whose measurements are represented, how errors are caught, and whether residents can understand the results. These are applied questions; the city resources below are not an AI policy.

readings.title: City of Bulverde Stormwater Management Program 2025–2029
readings.note: Sets out local measures to reduce runoff pollution and protect creeks and surface water.

readings.title: Environmental Data Portal
readings.note: Provides public access to regional environmental observations used in scientific research and policy decisions.

readings.title: Data Feminism
readings.source: Catherine D'Ignazio and Lauren F. Klein · MIT Press
readings.note: Shows how power and inequality shape data collection and analysis, and offers a framework for asking who is missing.

dc.intro: The District's AI Values Alignment handbook gives government teams a public framework for responsibility and transparency. As AI is used in public services, residents need to know when it informs decisions, which official remains accountable, and how to question its effects.

readings.title: Handbook for AI Values Alignment
readings.source: District of Columbia Office of the Chief Technology Officer
readings.note: The handbook asks agencies to align AI use with District values and keep responsibility for government action clear.

readings.title: Weapons of Math Destruction: How Big Data Increases Inequality and Threatens Democracy
readings.note: Explains how opaque, unaccountable scoring systems can harm people and distort public life.
